Using the newsroom¶

Readers, journalists and editors¶

Register as a reader to follow publishers and journalists. The reading list, article pages and newsletters show approved content only. Save subscriptions from the subscriptions screen; they determine your subscribed API feed and future approval notifications. The local mail backend prints messages in the server terminal rather than delivering email to real inboxes.

Register as a journalist to create articles and newsletters. Select only a publisher you belong to, or leave the publisher blank for independent work. You can change or delete your own work. Editing an approved article returns it to draft, so an editor must review it again before readers can see it.

Editors are assigned by a trusted administrator through /admin/. Public registration cannot grant this role. Editors can review drafts and approve, update or delete articles. Newsletter forms accept approved articles only. Making someone a Django superuser does not automatically give them the application’s editor role: set the role explicitly.

Approval and recovery¶

Approval is committed before an actual HTTP POST to the internal receiver. Subscribers to the journalist and publisher are combined without duplicates. Addresses are sent as BCC, not exposed to other readers. A persisted ledger tracks email and HTTP independently. Repeat the editor’s approval action to retry incomplete steps; an already recorded email success is not repeated.

A pending notification does not undo article approval. Check the delivery flags and error text in the read-only admin records. Verify the internal URL and matching server secret before retrying an HTTP error. Never paste that secret into a browser form, public issue, Git commit or API token response. SMTP cannot guarantee exactly-once delivery if the process crashes between sending a message and saving its completion flag.

API use¶

POST a registered username/password to /api/token/ to obtain a token. Send Authorization: Token YOUR_TOKEN on API requests. Obtain your own token at runtime; no shared credentials are bundled with the project.

  • GET /api/articles/: approved article list.

  • GET /api/articles/subscribed/: reader’s followed sources.

  • GET /api/articles/<id>/: visible article detail.

  • POST /api/articles/: journalist creates an article.

  • PUT / DELETE /api/articles/<id>/: authorised owner or editor.

  • POST /api/articles/<id>/approve/: editor-only approval and retry.

Clients cannot choose an author or directly set an approval flag. The internal /api/approved/ receiver requires the server secret and an already approved article; it is not a public route for bypassing approval.

Setup¶

The repository README contains the tested virtual-environment and Docker commands, environment-variable instructions, database health checks and troubleshooting. Use a separate local database when running the tests.
